text: MGM Resorts International, a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1986, operates as a holding company through its subsidiaries, functioning as a global gaming and entertainment company with domestic and international locations offering best-in-class hotels and casinos, state-of-the-art meeting and conference spaces, live and theatrical entertainment, a wide range of restaurant, nightlife, and retail options, and sports betting and online gaming operations. The company believes it operates some of the finest casino resorts worldwide and reinvests in its properties through renovations of hotel rooms, restaurants, entertainment, and other amenities to maintain a competitive edge. As of December 31, 2022, it operated 17 domestic casino resorts and, through its 56% controlling interest in MGM China Holdings Limited, which owns MGM Grand Paradise, S.A., operated two casino resorts in Macau. The company also has global online gaming operations via its consolidated subsidiary LeoVegas AB and its unconsolidated 50% owned venture, BetMGM, LLC. The domestic resorts’ real estate assets are leased under triple-net lease agreements. Prior to the VICI Transaction, MGM Growth Properties LLC (“MGP”) was a consolidated subsidiary and, through its subsidiary MGP OP, served as landlord for certain domestic properties under an intercompany master lease. In recent years, the company has pursued an asset-light business model to monetize real estate assets, redeploy capital, and focus on growth, particularly in U.S. online sports betting and iGaming through BetMGM, acquiring LeoVegas, expanding digital capabilities, and developing operations in Japan. Key transactions include: in July 2018, forming BetMGM with Entain plc, which received exclusive access to MGM’s land-based and online sports betting, major tournament poker, and online gaming operations and Entain’s U.S. technology; in January 2019, acquiring Empire City Casino’s racetrack and casino for approximately $865 million, with MGP later acquiring the developed real property and adding it to the master lease; in March 2019, amending the master lease with MGP related to Park MGM and NoMad Las Vegas rebranding; in November 2019, forming the Bellagio BREIT Venture (5% owned by a subsidiary of MGM and 95% by a subsidiary of Blackstone Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc.) that acquired the Bellagio real estate assets for $4.25 billion and leased them back; in December 2019, selling Circus Circus Las Vegas and adjacent land for $825 million; on February 14, 2020, contributing the real estate assets of MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay (including Mandalay Place) to the VICI BREIT Venture (50.1% owned by a subsidiary of MGP OP and 49.9% by a subsidiary of BREIT) for $4.6 billion, with the real estate leased back and the master lease modified to remove Mandalay Bay; on January 14, 2020, entering into a waiver agreement to redeem approximately 30 million MGP OP units for $700 million on May 18, 2020, and approximately 24 million MGP OP units for $700 million on December 2, 2020, terminating the waiver; on March 4, 2021, delivering a redemption notice to MGP for approximately 37 million MGP OP units, resulting in aggregate cash proceeds of about $1.2 billion, using cash on hand and proceeds from MGP’s issuance of Class A shares; on September 27, 2021, acquiring the remaining 50% ownership in CityCenter Holdings, LLC for $2.125 billion; on September 28, 2021, selling the real estate assets of Aria and Vdara to Blackstone funds for $3.89 billion and leasing them back to a subsidiary; on September 28, 2021, announcing selection by Osaka as the region’s integrated resort partner with ORIX Corporation, forming a venture to develop one of Japan’s first integrated resorts, and submitting an Area Development Plan to Japan’s central government on April 27, 2022; on October 29, 2021, MGP acquiring the real estate assets of MGM Springfield for $400 million and adding it to the master lease; on April 29, 2022, completing the VICI Transaction with VICI Properties, Inc. (“VICI”) and MGP, where MGP Class A shareholders received 1.366 shares of newly issued VICI stock for each MGP Class A share, and the company received 1.366 units of VICI Properties OP LLC (“VICI OP”) for each MGP OP unit held, with VICI OP redeeming the majority of the units and the company retaining approximately 1% ownership, MGP’s Class B shares held by the company were cancelled, and the company no longer holds a controlling interest in MGP, deconsolidating MGP upon closing; in connection with the VICI Transaction, an amended and restated master lease with VICI was entered into; on May 17, 2022, acquiring the operations of The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas for $1.625 billion plus working capital adjustments, totaling approximately $1.7 billion, and entering into a lease for its real estate; on September 7, 2022, acquiring LeoVegas through a tender offer at a cash price of SEK 61 per share, with a total fair value of equity interests acquired of approximately $556 million, inclusive of cash settlement of equity awards; on December 16, 2022, receiving a new gaming concession in Macau, effective January 1, 2023; on December 19, 2022, selling the operations of The Mirage to an affiliate of Seminole Hard Rock Entertainment, Inc. (“Hard Rock”) for $1.075 billion, subject to adjustments, and amending the master lease with VICI to remove The Mirage and reduce annual cash rent by $90 million; and on February 15, 2023, selling the operations of Gold Strike Tunica to CNE Gaming Holdings, LLC (“CNE”), a subsidiary of Cherokee Nation Business, for $450 million, subject to adjustments, and amending the master lease with VICI to remove Gold Strike Tunica and reduce annual cash rent by $40 million. All transactions with MGP, including those under the master lease, have been eliminated in consolidation. For further details on acquisitions, divestitures, venture transactions, and other arrangements, see “Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and the notes to the consolidated financial statements. The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the company’s business and recovery is discussed in “Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Description of our business and key performance indicators — Impact of COVID-19,” and risks related to the pandemic are detailed in “Item 1A. Risk Factors.”

On February 15, 2023, MGM Resorts completed the sale of the operations of Gold Strike Tunica to CNE Gaming Holdings, LLC (“CNE”), a subsidiary of Cherokee Nation Business, for a cash consideration of $450 million, subject to certain purchase price adjustments. At closing, the master lease with VICI was amended to remove Gold Strike Tunica and reflect a $40 million reduction in annual cash rent. For further details on this transaction, refer to Note 4. As of December 31, 2022, MGM Resorts had three reportable segments: Las Vegas Strip Resorts, Regional Operations, and MGM China. Las Vegas Strip Resorts includes Aria (including Vdara), Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan, MGM Grand Las Vegas (including The Signature), Mandalay Bay (including Delano and Four Seasons), The Mirage (until its disposition in December 2022), Luxor, New York-New York (including The Park), Excalibur, and Park MGM (including NoMad Las Vegas). Regional Operations includes MGM Grand Detroit, Beau Rivage, Gold Strike Tunica (until its disposition in February 2023), Borgata, MGM National Harbor, MGM Springfield, Empire City, and MGM Northfield Park. Over half of the net revenue from Las Vegas Strip Resorts comes from non-gaming operations such as hotel, food and beverage, entertainment, and other amenities, while the majority of net revenue from Regional Operations is derived from gaming operations. The company’s long-term strategy focuses on marketing to diverse customer segments and utilizing its convention and meeting facilities to maximize hotel occupancy and customer volumes, which improves labor utilization. Operating results are highly dependent on customer volume, which affects room pricing and other amenity charges. Casino operations offer a variety of slots and table games, with premium players accessing high-limit rooms and lounge experiences. MGM Resorts owns approximately 56% of MGM China, which owns and operates MGM Macau and MGM Cotai through MGM Grand Paradise, holding the relevant gaming and land concessions. Although visitation in 2020, 2021, and 2022 was significantly reduced by the COVID-19 pandemic, long-term growth in the Asian gaming market is expected to drive future visitation. MGM China’s revenues are primarily from gaming operations under a concession administered by the Macau Government. VIP gaming at MGM China uses special purpose nonnegotiable gaming chips, with commissions based on rolling chip turnover, recorded as a reduction of casino revenue; however, VIP gaming was not a significant source of revenue in 2022 and is not expected to be in future years. The majority of revenue comes from main floor gaming, which is expected to be the primary growth driver. The company suspended operations with its primary gaming promoters in December 2021, and prior to that, gaming promoters received revenue-sharing and allowances based on table games turnover. Key competitors in Macau include five other concessionaires, as well as major gaming centers in Singapore, South Korea, Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, Australia, and Las Vegas. Marketing efforts include advertising through radio, television, internet, billboards, newspapers, magazines, direct mail, email, and social media, as well as regional offices. MGM Rewards is a tiered loyalty program offering benefits such as priority access, exclusive events, and redemption for hotel stays, food, and other experiences, while the Golden Lion Club and M life Rewards are offered at MGM China. The company’s strategic plan centers on five pillars: Strong People and Culture, Customer-Centric Model, Operational Excellence, Disciplined Capital Allocation, and Gaming Entertainment. Key growth initiatives include developing an integrated resort in Japan, investing in BetMGM, expanding international digital opportunities through LeoVegas, and exploring full-scale commercial gaming at Empire City in New York. In September 2021, MGM and ORIX were selected by Osaka as the region’s integrated resort partner, and in April 2022, a development plan was submitted to the central government. BetMGM is positioned as a long-term leader in U.S. online sports betting and iGaming, with the MGM Rewards program integrated and BetMGM branded on-property at sportsbooks and kiosks. In January 2023, a request for application for three downstate commercial gaming licenses was released, to which MGM expects to respond. Technology is critical to enhancing customer experience, employee productivity, and operational efficiency, with a focus on creating unique content, fostering guest engagement, enabling cross-property promotions, and improving data-driven decision-making. A new loyalty technology platform allows customers to earn points from both gaming and non-gaming activities, with bundling capabilities to offer customized packages. MGM Resorts has a long-standing commitment to environmental and social responsibility, with a dedicated board committee on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and, since 2019, a unified Executive Committee-level leader overseeing Environmental Sustainability, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, Philanthropy, and Community Engagement through the MGM Resorts Social Impact and Sustainability Center of Excellence. In 2022, the company advanced its ESG reporting, aligning with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Global Reporting Initiative, and Sustainability Accounting Standards Board standards, and updated its website at mgmresorts.com/esg to present these disclosures. The year ended December 31, 2022 marked the first full calendar year of operation for the Mega Solar Array (“Mega Array”), which on average met or exceeded production expectations.

Our most recent Social Impact & Sustainability Report builds on the 2021 disclosures to show progress in public social impact and sustainability goals, with a new report scheduled for publication in 2023 to detail 2022 achievements. This reporting aligns with our first Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures report, released in May 2022, and complements disclosures under the Global Reporting Initiative and Sustainability Accounting Standards Board Hotels & Lodging and Casinos & Gaming Sector Standards. These disclosures are now presented on our website at mgmresorts.com/esg, which is for informational purposes only and not incorporated by reference into the Annual Report on Form 10-K. In 2022, the first full calendar year of operation for the Mega Solar Array, the system on average met or exceeded production expectations, supporting our climate goals: a 45% reduction in Scope 1 & 2 carbon emissions intensity (pounds of CO₂ equivalent per square foot; 2007 baseline) by 2025; a 50% reduction in absolute Scope 1 & 2 carbon emissions (metric tons of CO₂ equivalent; 2019 baseline) by 2030; and 100% renewable electricity purchased in the U.S. and 80% globally by 2030. We also committed to reducing value chain emissions by 30% across our significant Scope 3 categories by 2030. Our water strategy includes a global water policy developed in 2022 to promote responsible water use and stewardship, and we enhanced water disclosures by participating in the 2022 CDP Water Security Questionnaire, achieving an “A” rating, the highest possible. Our principal trademarks include Aria, Vdara, Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan, Borgata, Mandalay Bay, MGM, MGM Grand, MGM Resorts International, Luxor, Excalibur, New York-New York, Beau Rivage, Empire City, and LeoVegas, all registered or allowed in the U.S. and Europe, with additional trademarks like The Mirage registered or applied for in the U.S. and other foreign jurisdictions. These brand names are vital to our business, enhancing name recognition, reputation, and customer attraction, and are protected with perpetual duration as long as used and renewed. Our human capital strategy emphasizes a people-driven culture guided by core values: Captivate Our Audience, Inspire Excellence, Champion Inclusion, and Win Together, with a long-term plan to attract and develop talent to support business, guest experience, community engagement, and financial goals. We support local hiring, veteran programs, community training, internship and management development, and have streamlined recruitment to meet agile staffing needs. We invest in continuous learning, offering tuition reimbursement, student loan debt repayment, and partnerships with the Nevada System of Higher Education to allow employees to earn online degrees for free. New initiatives include a sabbatical program for director-level and above employees and enhanced employee recognition and onboarding programs. Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) approach is rooted in corporate and people strategies and social impact, guided by four pillars: invest in people, build an inclusive culture, grow business and customer engagement and supplier diversity, and enhance marketplace leadership and community relations. We have set four long-range 2025 goals: (1) equal access to leadership opportunities for all employees, (2) spending at least 10% of biddable procurement with diverse suppliers, (3) expanding the Supplier Diversity Mentorship Program to 150 graduates, and (4) training 100% of management employees on social impact and sustainability policies and goals. Each goal is tracked via key performance indicators, published in our annual report, and reviewed by management and the CSR & Sustainability Committee of the Board. Internal workforce reports with demographic and diversity data are regularly reviewed by the same committee, executive management, and leadership teams. Internal communication channels to advance Champion Inclusion include open executive forums, employee engagement surveys with action plans, and employee network groups. DE&I is advanced through employee training, community partnerships, recruitment, advocacy, outreach, and internal groups such as Supplier Diversity and ESG task forces, led by the Chief People, Inclusion and Sustainability Officer, who reports directly to the CEO and President, supported by a centralized Diversity and Inclusion team and HR. We promote employee health, safety, and wellness through benefits, tools, and digital resources, including the launch of World of Wellbeing (WOW), a holistic approach to employee wellness, and continued efforts to ensure health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our philanthropic focus is on Embracing Humanity and Protecting the Planet, through programs centered on caring for one another and investing in communities. The MGM Resorts Foundation, established in 2002, offers two types of grants: Employee Emergency Grants for employees and Community Grants for local communities. Employees are encouraged to volunteer through programs like VolunteerREWARDS, which allows them to earn grant money for their chosen nonprofit based on volunteer hours. As of December 31, 2022, we had approximately 46,000 full-time and 18,000 part-time employees domestically, 10,000 and 1,000 employees at MGM China and LeoVegas, respectively. We had collective bargaining agreements with unions covering approximately 38,000 employees, including agreements with the Local Joint Executive Board of Las Vegas for eight resorts and about 22,000 employees, expiring May 31, 2023, and other agreements expiring in 2023 at Beau Rivage, MGM Grand Detroit, MGM National Harbor, transportation units in Las Vegas, MGM Northfield Park, and various smaller units. Successor contract negotiations will begin as expiration dates approach and continue throughout 2023. Employees at MGM China and LeoVegas are not part of any labor union and are not bound by collective bargaining agreements. The gaming industry is highly regulated, requiring licenses and gaming taxes to operate, with extensive oversight under local laws concerning ownership, financial stability, and character. Violations in one jurisdiction may result in disciplinary action elsewhere. A detailed description of these regulations is in Exhibit 99.1, incorporated by reference. Our operations are also subject to federal, state, local, and foreign laws on alcoholic beverages, smoking, employees, currency, taxation, zoning, building codes (including ADA requirements), construction, land use, marketing, and advertising. We handle significant cash and are subject to anti-money laundering and reporting regulations, which could change or be interpreted differently, potentially affecting operations. We are also subject to environmental laws such as the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation Recovery Act, Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act, and the Oil Pollution Act of 1990. Owners or operators may be held liable for hazardous substances on property regardless of knowledge or responsibility, and no such issues have been identified that would adversely affect operations. For risks related to regulatory matters, see “Item 1A. Risk Factors — Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters and Changes in Public Policy.” This Form 10-K and the 2022 Annual Report contain forward-looking statements, including those about the impact of COVID-19, macroeconomic trends, strategic initiatives, capital expenditures, share repurchases, dividends, cost savings, deferred tax assets, and ESG goals. These statements are based on current expectations and are subject to uncertainties, risks, and changes, and actual results may differ materially. Important factors include substantial indebtedness, fixed rent payments, credit facility restrictions, high rent obligations, competition, economic conditions, dividend suspensions, lease risks, landlord challenges, concentration on the Las Vegas Strip, credit risk, goodwill impairments, geopolitical events, cybersecurity risks, reputational risks, failure to achieve ESG goals, climate change, water scarcity, regulatory compliance, anti-corruption laws, and gaming tax increases.

Our business faces several significant risks that could adversely affect its operations, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows. These include the impact of rising energy prices, which could harm our operating results; potential failures in future expansion efforts through investments, alliances, acquisitions, or divestitures; risks related to the integrity of our computer systems and internal customer data, which could damage our reputation and expose us to fines, lawsuits, or restrictions on data use; reputational harm due to increased scrutiny of our corporate social responsibility initiatives; the possibility of failing to achieve our ESG goals or realizing intended benefits from ESG initiatives; disruptions from extreme weather or climate change causing property damage or business interruptions; and water scarcity negatively affecting operations. Our businesses are subject to extensive regulation, and non-compliance or the cost of compliance could harm our operations. Risks associated with doing business outside the United States, including violations of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act or similar anti-corruption laws, also pose threats. Increases in gaming taxes and fees in operating jurisdictions could negatively affect financial results. The recognition of our foreign tax credit deferred tax asset is uncertain, and the valuation allowance applied against it may vary significantly in future periods. Changes in fiscal and tax policies, pending or future claims against us, and disruptions to our computer systems from cyber-attacks or other causes could impair our ability to serve customers and affect sales and operations. The global COVID-19 pandemic has continued to materially impact MGM China’s business, financial results, and liquidity, and this impact could worsen and persist for an unknown duration. We are restricted from having any interest or involvement in gaming businesses in mainland China, Macau, Hong Kong, or Taiwan, except through MGM China. The Macau government may terminate MGM Grand Paradise’s concession under certain circumstances without compensation, redeem the concession after the eighth year with at least one year’s prior notice and subject to payment of reasonable and fair damages or indemnity, or refuse to extend the concession in 2032. Additionally, conflicts of interest may arise because certain of our directors and officers also serve as directors of MGM China. As of December 31, 2022, we had approximately $8.8 billion of consolidated indebtedness outstanding, including $4.2 billion related to MGM China. Increases in interest rates on existing or future borrowings would raise the cost of debt and reduce available cash flow. We do not guarantee MGM China’s debt obligations, and our ability to make additional investments into MGM China is limited by covenants in our senior credit facility. We also provide shortfall guarantees for $3.01 billion and $3.0 billion of indebtedness of Bellagio BREIT Venture and VICI BREIT Venture, respectively, which could require us to fund material shortfalls after lenders exhaust remedies, potentially necessitating additional financing. MGM Grand Paradise is required to make investments in gaming and non-gaming projects, with non-gaming commitments increasing if Macau’s annual gross gaming revenue reaches a specified level; however, there is no assurance that MGM Grand Paradise will have sufficient cash or financing to meet these obligations, and failure to do so could result in the termination of its concession. Our operations are capital-intensive, requiring significant investments to maintain, modernize, and refurbish owned, leased, and managed resorts. Leases for these properties include fixed rental payments with annual escalators and require us to apply a percentage of net revenues to capital expenditures.

MGM Grand Paradise is subject to the risk that if it fails to meet its investment commitments, the Macau government may terminate its concession contract without compensation. The Macau government also has the right, starting from the eighth year of the concession, to redeem the concession with at least one year’s prior notice and subject to payment of reasonable and fair damages or indemnity, or to refuse to grant an extension of the concession in 2032. The company’s businesses are capital-intensive, requiring significant ongoing investments to maintain, modernize, and refurbish owned, leased, and managed resorts. Leases for these properties include fixed rental payments with annual escalators and require the company to apply a percentage of net revenues to capital expenditures. These investments demand a continuous supply of cash, which must be sourced from operations or through borrowing or other financing if not generated internally. Development projects, including potential future integrated resort developments in Japan, strategic initiatives such as positioning BetMGM as a leader in online sports betting and iGaming, growth in the international digital gaming business, and acquisitions, may require substantial capital commitments, additional debt, guarantees of third-party debt, or contingent liabilities, all of which could negatively impact the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. Current and future economic, capital, and credit market conditions could impair the company’s ability to service its substantial debt and meet significant financial commitments, including lease rent payments and planned expenditures. Cash flow generation, distributions from unconsolidated affiliates like MGM China, and access to the senior credit facility or new debt are critical to meeting these obligations. If economic conditions deteriorate—such as during a recession—consumer spending may decline, reducing revenues and cash flow, potentially leading to failure to meet debt or lease covenants. If such covenants are breached, future borrowings under the senior secured credit facility may not be available in sufficient amounts or on favorable terms, and access to capital markets may be limited. A significant portion of the company’s cash flows is required to pay rent under triple-net lease agreements, with an aggregate annual rent payment of $1.7 billion, subject to annual escalators. The leases also require capital expenditures and impose financial covenants: under the VICI lease, cash collateral or letters of credit equal to six or one year of rent (depending on circumstances) must be posted; under the Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand Las Vegas, Aria, Vdara, and The Cosmopolitan leases, one year of rent; and under the Bellagio lease, two years of rent. These obligations may make it harder to meet debt obligations, increase vulnerability to economic downturns, reduce cash flow available for working capital, capital expenditures, development, dividends, share repurchases, and other corporate purposes, limit flexibility in responding to business or industry changes, restrict major transactions like acquisitions or divestitures, and result in loss of rights to the leased properties upon default. The company faces intense competition in destination travel, hotel, resort, entertainment, and gaming industries, including from online sports betting and iGaming, which could reduce customer visitation and spending at land-based properties. BetMGM, the company’s venture in online sports betting and iGaming, faces significant competition and may fail to achieve the scale needed to compete effectively, reducing anticipated returns from the investment. Expansion of iGaming and online sports betting in the U.S. and abroad may further compete with land-based operations. Increased competition could arise from new gaming establishments closer to customers or from new gaming licenses in jurisdictions like Japan, Taiwan, or Thailand. MGM Grand Paradise holds one of only six gaming concessions authorized by the Macau government, and if additional concessions are granted or existing operators open new facilities, competition will increase. The Macau Gaming Inspection and Co-ordination Bureau’s increased scrutiny and restrictions on gaming promoters have led the company to suspend its primary gaming promoters, resulting in significant revenue declines. This has heightened competition in the mass market segment, and failure to maintain or grow this business or replace revenue from gaming promoters could harm the company’s financial performance. Most jurisdictions with casino gaming impose numerical or geographical limits on new licenses, and even if new opportunities arise, competition for them—such as through acquisitions—will be intense. The company also competes with travel destinations outside its markets. Its business is sensitive to reductions in discretionary consumer spending and corporate spending on conventions and business events. Adverse macroeconomic conditions, inflation, economic uncertainty, or consumer perceptions of weak economic conditions can reduce demand for luxury amenities and travel. Changes in consumer preferences, such as a growing demand for non-gaming offerings, may affect performance, particularly at Aria, Bellagio, MGM Grand Las Vegas, and The Cosmopolitan, which are affected by economic conditions in the Far East, and all Nevada resorts by U.S. and California economic conditions. A recession or economic slowdown could reduce visitation and harm operating results. Adverse market conditions may also disrupt the labor market and global supply chains, impacting the company’s ability to hire and retain employees or procure supplies. The company’s operations in Macau are also affected by competition for labor, with Macau government policies limiting the import of certain workers—such as casino dealers—potentially increasing labor costs. As more gaming and non-gaming projects open, transportation infrastructure in Macau may become strained, and inadequate facilities could reduce Macau’s appeal and negatively impact operations. The company has suspended its regular dividends, effective February 8, 2023, to focus on share repurchases, and there is no assurance that dividends will resume in the foreseeable future or at all, due to factors including the holding company structure, debt agreements, state law, liquidity, alternative uses of cash, and economic conditions. All domestic gaming facilities are leased under triple-net leases that require the company to pay rent, facility maintenance, insurance, taxes (excluding those on the lessor’s income), capital expenditures, and utilities, regardless of property performance or events like casualty or condemnation. These obligations are absolute, and the leases restrict the company’s ability to cease operations at its properties, except under limited circumstances. Because a significant number of the company’s major gaming resorts are located on the Las Vegas Strip, they are particularly exposed to regional market dynamics.

All of our domestic properties are subject to triple-net leases that require us to pay, in addition to rent: (1) all facility maintenance, (2) all insurance required for the leased properties and the business conducted there, (3) taxes levied on or with respect to the leased properties (excluding taxes on the income of the lessor), (4) all capital expenditures, and (5) all utilities and other services necessary or appropriate for the leased properties and the business. These obligations are absolute in virtually all circumstances, regardless of property performance or events such as casualty or condemnation that might otherwise abate rent in traditional leases, and our leases limit our ability to cease operations at these properties, with only limited exceptions. Because a significant number of our major gaming resorts are located on the Las Vegas Strip, we face greater risks than a more geographically diversified gaming company. Our business is particularly vulnerable to risks common in the Las Vegas tourism industry, such as changes in air service availability and disruptions to air travel, which we rely on for a large portion of our visitors. Reductions in flights by major airlines due to higher fuel prices, lower demand, or other factors can reduce visitor numbers. Additionally, there is one principal interstate highway between Las Vegas and Southern California, where many of our customers reside; capacity constraints or traffic disruptions on this route may also reduce customer visits. We extend credit to a large portion of our customers through the issuance of unsecured markers, with table game players and high-end players typically receiving more markers than others. High-end gaming is more volatile and can significantly impact cash flow and earnings in a quarter; the loss or reduction in play by a major high-end customer could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. We issue markers only to customers whose play level and financial resources, in management’s judgment, justify credit extension. Uncollectible receivables from high-end customers could significantly affect our results. While gaming debts evidenced by markers and judgments on such debts are enforceable under Nevada law and enforceable in all U.S. states under the Full Faith and Credit Clause, other jurisdictions may deem enforcement of gaming debts contrary to public policy. Courts in some foreign nations may enforce gaming debts directly and reach U.S. assets of foreign debtors, but U.S. court judgments are not binding in many foreign nations. MGM China expects to enforce its gaming debts only in limited jurisdictions, including Macau; for customers from other jurisdictions, MGM China may not have access to forums where it can collect all receivables due to the non-enforceability of gaming debts in many jurisdictions. Under applicable law, MGM China remains obligated to pay taxes on uncollectible winnings. Even where gaming debts are enforceable, they may not be collectible, and our inability to collect such debts could significantly harm our operating results. We review goodwill, indefinite-lived intangible assets, and long-lived assets annually and during interim periods in accordance with authoritative guidance. Past write-downs and impairment charges have resulted from significant negative trends, reduced future cash flow estimates, business disruptions, slower growth, or lack of growth; future events could require additional impairment charges, which would materially adversely affect our consolidated results of operations. Leisure and business travel, especially by air, are highly susceptible to global geopolitical events such as terrorist attacks, acts of violence, war, or the outbreak of infectious diseases like COVID-19. Since most of our customers travel by air to our Las Vegas and Macau properties, any terrorist act, violence, outbreak of hostilities, or perceived threat to air travel could negatively affect our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. Although we have obtained some insurance for certain terrorist acts, coverage for physical loss or business interruption from war and some forms of terrorism remains unavailable. Co-investing in properties or businesses, including our investment in BetMGM, reduces our ability to manage risk. As co-investors, we share control over operations, and disagreements—such as on capital contributions—could arise. If we and Entain cannot support BetMGM’s future funding, it may lack resources to implement its strategies, including market share growth, which could reduce our anticipated benefits. If we are awarded a concession to develop an integrated casino resort in Japan, we would do so in a consortium with ORIX and other local investors, which could limit our control over development activities, timing, or completion, potentially impacting our timeline or ability to meet specifications. Any future construction, development, or expansion projects—such as our proposed resort in Japan or full-scale gaming at Empire City—are subject to significant risks, including: lack of financing or delays in availability, changes in plans or specifications, engineering problems, shortages or price increases in energy, materials, and labor, wage inflation, delays in obtaining permits or licenses, changes in gaming, leisure, real estate, or construction regulations, labor disputes, availability of qualified contractors, disputes with contractors, personal injuries, environmental or health and safety issues, weather delays, fires, typhoons, geological or construction problems, and other unanticipated circumstances. These risks could increase costs, delay or prevent project completion, or alter design and features. Regulatory approvals may require us to open future casino resorts by specific deadlines; failure to meet these deadlines without extension could result in loss of approval or penalties, negatively affecting our business. We make significant capital expenditures to maintain and upgrade resorts, which may disrupt operations and displace revenue, including during renovations of rooms, restaurants, and meeting spaces. Our insurance coverage may not be sufficient to cover all possible losses. While we have “all risk” property insurance covering damage from fire, natural disasters, or terrorism, each policy has exclusions, and coverage amounts may be significantly less than the expected replacement cost in the event of total loss. Certain events—such as labor strikes, nuclear events, acts of war, loss of income due to canceled reservations or fear of terrorism, loss of power, deterioration, insect or animal damage, and pollution—are not covered. This could expose us to substantial uninsured losses. Business interruption and general liability insurance may not fully cover losses from such events, and our leases for the MGM Grand Las Vegas & Mandalay Bay, Bellagio, Aria & Vdara, and The Cosmopolitan require specified insurance coverage. We cannot guarantee we will continue to obtain such coverage at commercially reasonable costs or at all, and failure to do so could require lease amendments or result in default, materially harming our business. We renew insurance policies annually, and rising costs may force us to reduce policy limits, increase deductibles, or accept exclusions. Failure to protect our trademarks could harm the value of our brand and negatively affect our business. While our business is not substantially dependent on any single trademark, we actively file and obtain trademark protection in the U.S. and foreign countries. Despite these efforts, parties may infringe our trademarks, and rights may be invalidated or unenforceable. Some foreign countries offer less protection for intellectual property, and monitoring unauthorized use is difficult. Litigation to enforce rights or determine validity may be necessary, resulting in substantial costs and resource diversion. We cannot assure that our efforts to protect trademarks will fully prevent imitation, which could diminish brand value, market acceptance, and competitive advantages. A significant portion of our labor force—approximately 38,000 employees as of December 31, 2022—is covered by collective bargaining agreements, most of which expire in 2023. Prolonged disputes, strikes, or labor unrest could harm operations and damage our reputation, while wage or benefit increases from new agreements could negatively impact results. The company’s primary business involves operating casino resorts offering gaming, hotel, convention, dining, entertainment, retail, and other resort amenities. Most revenue is cash-based, and the company relies on operating cash flow to pay rent, fund capital expenditures, repay debt, and return capital to shareholders. The company leases domestic resort real estate under triple-net lease agreements and invests in property improvements, including new hotel rooms, restaurants, entertainment, and amenities. It also offers online gaming and sports betting through LeoVegas and BetMGM. Results of operations are influenced by capital allocation, access to capital, and cost of capital, with a focus on maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning capital while pursuing strategic development. Operations are not highly seasonal, though results can vary due to major conventions, Far East baccarat volumes, marketing timing, holiday play, and customer segments, particularly high-end gaming customers. The spread of COVID-19 significantly impacted the company’s business, financial condition, and operations in 2020, 2021, and 2022. In March 2020, all domestic properties were temporarily closed due to government restrictions, with re-openings occurring through the second and third quarters of 2020, followed by gradual removal of restrictions by the end of 2021. By December 31, 2022, all domestic properties were open, though early 2022 saw reduced visitation due to the omicron variant. In Macau, operations resumed on February 20, 2020, with health safeguards, and travel restrictions remained in place, including visa requirements and quarantines, which limited visitation. In the third and fourth quarters of 2021, local cases led to a state of immediate prevention, mass testing, and closures, with gaming suspended on July 11, 2022, resuming on July 23, 2022, under health safeguards. On October 30, 2022, a case linked to MGM Cotai led to isolation of guests and staff and a suspension of all operations until November 1, 2022, with limited operations resuming on November 3, 2022. Travel visa applications resumed on November 1, 2022, though restrictions remained, impacting visitation. Starting in December 2022, Macau and mainland China began easing testing and quarantine requirements under the “dynamic zero” policy. On January 8, 2023, Macau lifted most travel and quarantine restrictions, with only overseas visitors from outside mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan required to present a negative test result until February 6, 2023, when all remaining restrictions were removed. Las Vegas visitor volume increased 21% year-over-year in 2022, driven by expanded convention, sporting, music, and entertainment events. In contrast, Macau visitor arrivals declined 26% year-over-year due to ongoing travel and entry restrictions. MGP OP issued approximately 3 million MGP OP units to the company representing 5% of the equity value, and the company provided a shortfall guarantee for VICI BREIT Venture’s debt.
